content:
#37525 and #37544 move Coloring.lean/ConcreteColorings.lean/EdgeLabeling.lean to a new Coloring/ folder, and a few naming suggestions surfaced. What do you think?
Feel free to add more options or more polls.

(btw, "list coloring" means that for each object you're coloring, you get a list of possible colors for it, instead of the color choices being global. Think of graph-coloring the world map, but with the constraint that the color of each country has to come from its own flag. k-list-colorable is often called k-choosable.)
("total coloring" is a coloring of vertices & edges simultaneously)

/poll Names for the modules of the different types of colorings
Coloring/{VertexColoring, EdgeColoring, VertexListColoring, EdgeListColoring, TotalColoring, TotalListColoring}
Coloring/{Vertex, Edge, VertexList, EdgeList, Total, TotalList}
Coloring/{Vertex, Edge, ListVertex, ListEdge, Total, ListTotal}
Coloring/{Vertices, Edges, VerticesList, EdgesList, Total, TotalList}
Coloring/{Vertices, Edges, ListVertices, ListEdges, Total, ListTotal}

/poll Name for ConcreteColorings.lean
Coloring/ConcreteColorings
Coloring/Concrete
Coloring/Constructions
Coloring/Examples
cc @ooovi @Yaël Dillies
Yaël Dillies Could you explain your reasons to not wanting the module names to match the types they are about, compared to Walks/ vs Walk/? Is it because they're files and not folders?
I just dislike the duplication of Coloring in the name. I would also be happy to remove the folder instead
Ultimately, the current new names are okay
Is the colouring library set up to handle vertex labellings satisfying arbitrary predicates on their neighbourhoods or is it only set up for proper colourings?
Context: I am dealing with a class of problems called locally checkable labellings which are generic labelling problems on graph vertices/edges (proper vertex colouring is one of them).
The current definition of coloring is only proper colorings
In that case I pick option 2. Otherwise I might have suggested the name Labelling instead of colouring.
If this is still open for discussion, I would like to suggest using the word "labelling" instead of coloring, since the latter is a special case of the former.
Using it where?
In the colouring module names?
But they are about coloring, not labeling
Yes but colorings are labellings
They're also functions but I presume you're not suggesting we use the word "Function". Could you elaborate?
We have SimpleGraph.EdgeLabeling already, this thread is specifically for discussion of the Lean names about colourings of graphs, not labellings of graphs.

Okay then colourings it is. In general there are all sorts of labelling problems that only differ from each other by the constraints imposed on the labellings in question. Dominating sets, vertex covers, independent sets, weak colourings, list colourings etc.

Shreyas Srinivas said:

Okay then colourings it is. In general there are all sorts of labelling problems that only differ from each other by the constraints imposed on the labellings in question. Dominating sets, vertex covers, independent sets, weak colourings, list colourings etc.

Indeed - in my formalisation of locally checkable labellings as we discussed in the past, these were all supported. For mathlib, we can talk about edge labellings, and vertex labellings are simply functions. For any other kind of constrained labellings, you can simply add predicates on the labellings in question, and this is how mathlib colourings and LCLs should be handled. However this thread is for the case of colourings and list colourings.
